description:
Trigger: ServerName::ip_address("fe80::") or any IPv6 textual form ending in '::' that is not bare '::'.

Bad behavior: returns IdentityError::MalformedInput. Affected forms include 'fe80::' (link-local self), '2001:db8::', '::ffff:0:0' inverted, and any well-formed RFC 5952 address ending in a zero-run.

Root cause: pkix-identity/src/lib.rs:725-738. When the loop encounters an empty part from split(':') and sets zero_run_at = Some(...), it only breaks on iter.peek().is_none(). For input 's = "fe80::"', split(':') yields ["fe80", "", ""]. After consuming the middle empty, peek returns Some(&"") (the trailing empty), so the loop continues, sees the second empty, and returns None on the multiple-'::' guard.

Fix: when an empty part is consumed in the loop body and the NEXT part is also empty (or iterator is exhausted), treat it as the trailing '::' terminator and break. Or: normalize the input by handling trailing-'::' the same way the leading-'::' branch is special-cased at line 713-720.

Verification: an existing test (parse_ipv6 unit-tested via ServerName::ip_address) does not cover trailing '::' — add tests for 'fe80::', '2001:db8::', and 'a:b:c:d:e:f:0::' to lock in.

Security impact: lower than the leading/middle cases — an SAN entry with a trailing-'::' IPv6 address cannot be matched even by a correctly-formed target. Operationally, fe80:: link-local SANs would silently fail to match. No misvalidation in the unsafe direction (Ok where it should be Err).
title: parse_ipv6 rejects trailing '::' forms ('fe80::', '2001:db8::')
